text:
alex: heads up — onboarding 'sable-m-int4' canary. noticing structured toolcall outputs flip between an array-form and an object-form depending on prompt language (en vs zh). samples below.

li: can you paste a couple of raw responses? timestamps + model config would help.

alex: sure — run with prompt '请提取实体' -> returns:
```
{"tool_call": ["open_file", {"path":"/etc/hosts"}]}
```
but with english prompt 'extract entities' ->
```
{"tool_call": {"name":"open_file","args":{"path":"/etc/hosts"}}}
```

noah: wtf. that's a schema shape flip. looks like generation prefers compact array when token budget tight? maybe decoder tail pruning in quantized mode.

maya: Also seen ionic tokenization differences for zh — multibyte tokens change decoding logits. Try running canary with tokenizer debug + seed.

alex: did that: tokenizer debug shows different tokenization boundaries leading to early eos in some samples. but not 100% correlated.

li: action items: (1) run mirror canary (run both int4 and fp16) on same prompts across en/zh and diff outputs, (2) add a schema-tolerant pre-parse that converts [name, args] arrays to object form, (3) add structured-output eval metric to detect shape flips in bulk.

noah: +1 on schema-tolerant pre-parse. Also lower retry backoff so parser can request a short regen instead of applying heuristic by default.

alex: created a quick script and dropped into /tmp/canary-diffs.log and kicked off mirror run. infra-bot: can you pin the job id?

infra-bot: job started: canary-run-7234567890-01, mirror mode: int4 vs fp16. ETA ~15m :hourglass:

maya: if we see >0.2% shape-flip rate we should block int4 rollout for structured toolcalls. logging: capture token-level logits + prefix tokens for failures.

li: noted. I'll add a lightweight parser that warns but doesn't block for now. set an alert if rate>0.02% per hour.

alex: thanks. will post results when the run finishes.

infra-bot: job finished: canary-run-7234567890-01 — summary: 0.45% shape flips on int4 vs 0.01% on fp16. artifacts: s3://redwood-canary/7234567890/diff.tar.gz

noah: that's beyond threshold. rollback plan? suggest fallback policy: integer-quant model uses fp16 for toolcall routes for now.

maya: agree. also start a small eval with schema-agnostic prompts to see if we can rewrite prompts that reduce flips (template engineering).

alex: opened PR #1842 to add fallback routing + parser sanitizer. assigning to @li for parser and @maya for prompt tests.

li: ack. I'll also add a canary metric to console dashboard.

alex: cool. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
